author: Akien
prose: for now, only graph trees are in postgres. and logs are indeed the very next thing we have to look at. because we don't have any. and we should have lots. the basemost class group is supposed to have a logging tool in it. and every single everyting is supposed to log major boundry crossings and state changes. that doesn't mean every function call, or every heartbeat from the ground loop... but starting an inference call sure should. a probe firing at a gate crossing should. the logs are the picture of what just happened when we have a problem. so given where we seem to be, before we switch to opus, we should have you review this. because i went straight from ground loop to things much higher up because i was an idiot and just assumed this part was working. in ~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/<whatever else> so the path mirrors the code tree. why? easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go. we have a skill that's supposed to help you with a prebuild step for debugging instead of code writing. it's supposed to operate on that logging tree. [mid-review addendum, same conversation, on being shown the two existing breadcrumb trails:] indeed, perhaps i just didn't know where to look (about missing logs)
